messages.text:
You are watching a short video, shown as 24 frames sampled uniformly in time (frame 1 is the start, frame 24 is the end).

How to judge camera motion. Use the ground pattern, the horizon, and objects that are resting. Objects can move on their own, so do not decide from one moving object.
- Static (not moving): the ground pattern, the horizon and every resting object stay in the same place in the image from the first frame to the last. Only objects that move on their own change position.
- Turning in place (panning): the whole view slides sideways as one piece. Near and far things shift by the same amount, nothing changes size, and new scenery enters at one edge while old scenery leaves at the other.
- Orbiting around the scene: the camera travels sideways around a centre point while facing it. Near things shift more than far things, so resting objects slide against the background, the ground pattern appears to rotate or shear, and sides of objects hidden at the start may come into view.
- Moving straight toward or away from the scene: everything grows (toward) or shrinks (away), spreading from or gathering toward the image centre. Near objects change size faster than far ones. The view does not slide sideways.
The camera can be static while objects move, and it can move while every object rests.

How to judge camera motion. Use the ground pattern, the horizon, and objects that are resting. Objects can move on their own, so do not decide from one moving object.
- Static (not moving): the ground pattern, the horizon and every resting object stay in the same place in the image from the first frame to the last. Only objects that move on their own change position.
- Turning in place (panning): the whole view slides sideways as one piece. Near and far things shift by the same amount, nothing changes size, and new scenery enters at one edge while old scenery leaves at the other.
- Orbiting around the scene: the camera travels sideways around a centre point while facing it. Near things shift more than far things, so resting objects slide against the background, the ground pattern appears to rotate or shear, and sides of objects hidden at the start may come into view.
- Moving straight toward or away from the scene: everything grows (toward) or shrinks (away), spreading from or gathering toward the image centre. Near objects change size faster than far ones. The view does not slide sideways.
The camera can be static while objects move, and it can move while every object rests.
